rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zayd was called Zayd ibn Muhammad; after the Prophet married Zaynab, formerly married to Zayd ibn Haritha, Jews and hypocrites objected that he married his son's wife.
rows.anchor: يعني زيدا فكان يدعى زيد بن محمد فلما تزوج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم زينب بنت جحش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An adopted person is not truly the adopter's child, and the claim of sonship by adoption has no standing with God.
rows.anchor: ما جعل الله من تدعونه ولدا وهو ثابت النسب من غيركم ولدا لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling an adopted person a man's son is only something said aloud, without reality before God, who states the truth and guides to it.
rows.anchor: أن قولكم الدعي ابن الرجل شيء تقولونه بألسنتكم لا حقيقة له عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wife is not made a mother by zihar, just as an adopted person is not made a son by adoption.
rows.anchor: وهو أن الزوجة لا تصير بالظهار وأما والدعي لا يصير بالتبني ابنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Children should be attributed to their biological fathers, or to the men whose marital beds they were born in.
rows.anchor: الذين ولدوهم وانسبوهم إليهم أو إلى من ولدوا على فراشهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing people to their real fathers is the fairest statement and judgment before God.
rows.anchor: أي أعدل عند الله قولا وحكما

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar said they called Zayd ibn Haritha Zayd ibn Muhammad until this verse was revealed; al-Bukhari recorded the report in his Sahih.
rows.anchor: وروى سالم عن ابن عمر قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When their fathers' identities are unknown, call them brothers in the faith.
rows.anchor: أي لم تعرفوا بأعيانهم { فإخوانكم في الدين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains mawali here as paternal cousins.
rows.anchor: { ومواليكم } أي بنو أعمامكم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj allows mawali to mean allies in religion, who owe one another support.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: ويجوز أن يكون المراد أوليائكم في الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that mawali are the freedmen of people who emancipated them, to whom their wala belongs.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه معتقوكم ومحرروكم إذا اعتقتموهم من رق فلكم ولاؤهم.

words: وَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌۭ فِيمَآ أَخْطَأْتُم بِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no blame for mistakenly attributing someone to an adoptive father when one believes he is the biological father and does not know otherwise.
rows.anchor: في نسبته إلى المتبني إذا ظننتم أنه أبوه ولم تعلموا أنه ليس بابن له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People are accountable for deliberately attributing someone to someone other than his father.
rows.anchor: في الذي تعمدته قلوبكم وقصدتموه من دعائهم إلى غير آبائهم

words: وَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌۭ فِيمَآ أَخْطَأْتُم بِهِۦ
rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid distinguishes mistakes made before the prohibition from deliberate attribution after it.
rows.anchor: ما أخطأتم قبل النهي وما تعمدتموه بعد النهي عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God forgives what people said before and is merciful to them.
rows.anchor: لما سلف من قولكم { رحيما } بكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse establishes that claiming a lineage to someone other than one's father is impermissible; the Sunnah strongly warns against it.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه الآية دلالة على أنه لا يجوز الانتساب إلى غير الأب وقد وردت السنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Sunnah report curses whoever claims a father or patron other than his own.
rows.anchor: من انتسب إلى غير أبيه أو انتمى إلى غير مواليه فعليه لعنة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage supplies a formula asking God to bless Muhammad and his family as He blessed Abraham and his family, and to bless them likewise.
rows.anchor: قولوا اللهم صل على محمد وآل محمد كما صليت على إبراهيم وآل إبراهيم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud urged people to offer a beautiful prayer for the Prophet, since they did not know whether it would be presented to him, and taught a prayer invoking blessings and his praiseworthy station.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: إذا صليتم على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ وَمَلَٰٓئِكَتَهُۥ يُصَلُّونَ عَلَى ٱلنَّبِىِّ
rows.speaker: أبو بصير
rows.claim: Abu Basir reports Abu Abdillah explaining God's prayer for the Messenger as God's purification of him in the highest heavens.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بصير قال: سألت أبا عبد الله ع عن هذه الآية

rows.speaker: أبو بصير
rows.claim: Abu Abdillah explained taslim as submitting to the Prophet in matters.
rows.anchor: فقلت قد عرفت صلواتنا عليه فكيف التسليم فقال: هو التسليم له في الأمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this explanation, believers submit to the Prophet's commands and exert themselves in obeying everything he orders.
rows.anchor: انقادوا لأوامره وابذلوا الجهد في طاعته وفي جميع ما يأمركم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative is to greet the Prophet with a supplication, saying, Peace be upon you, Messenger of God.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه سلموا عليه بالدعاء أي قولوا: السلام عليك يا رسول الله

rows.speaker: أبو طلحة
rows.claim: Abu Talha, related by Anas ibn Malik, says the Prophet told him that one prayer upon him earns ten divine blessings, erases ten sins, and adds ten good deeds.
rows.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك عن أبي طلحة قال: دخلت على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view identifies those harming God and His Messenger as hypocrites, unbelievers, and people who attribute improper things to God or deny His messengers; harming God means disobeying Him or describing Him improperly, since God cannot literally be harmed.
rows.anchor: قيل: هم المنافقون والكافرون والذين وصفوا الله بما لا يليق به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation of harming God is blaspheming His names and attributes.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يؤذون الله يلحدون في أسمائه وصفاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view takes the phrase to mean harming the Messenger; God is named first to honor him, treating harm to the Messenger as harm to God.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه يؤذون رسول الله فقدم ذكر الله على وجه التعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage connects to the prayer command in the preceding verse: pray for the Prophet and do not harm him, since whoever harms him is an unbeliever.
rows.anchor: واتصاله بما قبله أنه كأنه يقول صلوا عليه ولا تؤذوه فإن من آذاه فهو كافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's curse means exclusion from His mercy and the arrival of punishment: loss of further guidance in this life and eternal fire in the next.
rows.anchor: أي يبعدهم الله من رحمته ويحل بهم وبال نقمته بحرمان زيادات الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised punishment in the afterlife humiliates them.
rows.anchor: في الآخرة { عذابا مهينا } أي مذلا لهم

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet said that whoever harms even one hair of Ali harms him, and whoever harms him harms God and incurs God's curse.
rows.anchor: قال: حدثني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author invokes 21:28, which limits intercession to those God approves, to refute unbelievers who worship idols as intermediaries that bring them near God.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال سبحانه ذلك لأن الكفار كانوا يقولون نعبدهم ليقربونا إلى الله زلفى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that fear is removed from their hearts.
rows.anchor: أي كشف الفزع عن قلوبهم وفزع كشف الله الفزع عن قلوبهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: One view says the pronoun refers to the idolaters: once fear is lifted they hear the angels, ask what their Lord said, and answer the truth, acknowledging the messengers; Ibn Abbas, Qatada, and Ibn Zayd report this.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس وقتادة وابن زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun refers to angels: when they ascend with human deeds, their loud sound makes others fear the Hour and prostrate, then ask what God said once reassured.
rows.anchor: أن الملائكة إذا صعدوا بأعمال العباد ولهم زجل وصوت عظيم فتحسب الملائكة أنها الساعة

rows.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
rows.claim: A second angelic explanation says that at Muhammad's mission Gabriel's descent with revelation frightened angels who thought the Hour had arrived; he calmed them as he passed through the heavens, and they learned the revelation was truth.
rows.anchor: قالوا الحق يعني الوحي عن مقاتل والكلبي

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: A third angelic account says angels faint and prostrate when God reveals to one of them; after they recover they ask what He said and learn it concerns others. Al-Jubba'i selects this explanation.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود واختاره الجبائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿAli means the sovereign, powerful, obeyed Lord; alternatively it means exalted in His attributes, while al-Kabir refers to His power.
rows.anchor: أي السيد القادر المطاع. وقيل: العلي في صفاته { الكبير } في قدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question forces unbelievers to concede that their idols cannot provide for them; the answer is God, who provides from the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: فإنهم لا يمكنهم أن يقولوا ترزقنا آلهتنا التي نعبدها ثم عند ذلك

words: وَإِنَّآ أَوْ إِيَّاكُمْ لَعَلَىٰ هُدًى أَوْ فِى ضَلَٰلٍ مُّبِينٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The either-or wording is fair-minded argument, not doubt: a speaker may say one of us is wrong while knowing who is wrong.
rows.anchor: إنما قال ذلك على وجه الإنصاف في الحجاج دون الشك كما يقول القائل لغيره أحدنا كاذب

rows.speaker: أبو الأسود الدؤلي
rows.claim: Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali's poem says that if loving the Prophet's family is right, he has attained it; he knows their love is guidance, so the conditional wording is no expression of doubt.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا يقول أبو الأسود الدؤلي يمدح أهل البيت ع:

words: وَإِنَّآ أَوْ إِيَّاكُمْ لَعَلَىٰ هُدًى أَوْ فِى ضَلَٰلٍ مُّبِينٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation combines both possible claims and leaves reason to distinguish them, effectively saying, I am guided and you are astray.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه جمع بين الخبرين وفوض التمييز إلى العقول

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: The poet's pairing of fresh and dried bird hearts with dates illustrates combining alternatives in one expression.
rows.anchor: كأن قلوب الطير رطبا ويابسا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls it an especially effective gentle appeal: the truthful speaker attributes guidance to himself and error to his opponent without bluntly accusing him, prompting reflection.
rows.anchor: وهذا من أحسن ما ينسب به المحق نفسه إلى الهدى وخصمه إلى الضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the unbelievers reject the argument, Muhammad is to say they are not asked about our sins, nor we about their deeds; each person is judged for his own actions.
rows.anchor: أيها الكفار { عما أجرمنا } أي اقترفنا من المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows that no one may be taken to account for another person's sin.
rows.anchor: بل كل إنسان يسأل عما يعمله ويجازي على فعله دون فعل غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every lifespan is recorded in the Preserved Tablet before it occurs; Sa'id ibn Jubayr says the lifespan is written in the Mother of the Book and its days are successively crossed off.
rows.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير مكتوب في أم الكتاب عمر فلان كذا سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving one person a long life, shortening another's, and recording it are all easy for God.
rows.anchor: يعني أن تعمير من يعمره ونقصان من ينقصه وإثبات ذلك في الكتاب سهل على الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The fresh water is pleasant and cold, and its drink passes easily and agreeably through the throat; Ibn Abbas describes the other sea as intensely salty.
rows.anchor: أي طيب بارد { سائغ شرابه } أي جائز في الحلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rest of the verse's explanation is given in the commentary on Sura al-Nahl.
rows.anchor: وما بعد هذا مفسر في سورة النحل إلى آخر الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes night enter day and day enter night through their increasing and decreasing, and directs the sun and moon as He wills until an appointed time.
rows.anchor: { يولج الليل في النهار ويولج النهار في الليل } أي يدخل أحدهما في الآخر بالزيادة والنقصان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God administers these matters, is their creator, and possesses dominion in this world and the next.
rows.anchor: { ذلكم الله ربكم } أي مدبر هذه الأمور هو الله خالقكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ones invoked besides God are idols and images that people worship.
rows.anchor: أي تدعونهم آلهة من الأصنام والأوثان وتوجهون عبادتكم إليهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Qitmir is the thin membrane on a date pit; the idols have power over neither little nor much, according to Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: أي قشر نواة عن ابن عباس أي لا يقدرون من ذلك على قليل ولا كثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols cannot hear pleas for relief because they are inanimate and can neither benefit nor harm; even if God gave them hearing, they could not respond.
rows.anchor: { لا يسمعوا دعاءكم } لأنها جماد لا تنفع ولا تضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Resurrection God makes the idols speak to rebuke their worshippers and disown their worship, saying they never asked to be worshipped.
rows.anchor: ينطقهم الله يوم القيامة لتوبيخ عابديها فيقولون لم عبدتمونا وما دعوناكم إلى ذلك

rows.speaker: البلخي
rows.claim: Al-Balkhi allows the referent to be angels or Jesus: they do not hear the worshippers, or are too occupied to attend to them.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المراد به الملائكة وعيسى

rows.speaker: البلخي
rows.claim: Al-Balkhi also allows the referent to be idols: their disavowal manifests the worshippers' mistaken belief, as inert things glorify God by showing evidence of Him.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المراد به الأصنام ويكون ما يظهر من بطلان ما ظنوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God, who knows everything, can fully inform of what brings benefit or harm and what is good or corrupting.
rows.anchor: أي لا يخبرك بما فيه الصلاح والفساد والمنافع والمضار مثل الله سبحانه العليم بالأشياء كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People are needy before God, while He has no need of their worship.
rows.anchor: { إلى الله والله هو الغني } عن عبادتكم لا يحتاج إلى شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God deserves praise for all His acts and does only what merits praise.
rows.anchor: المستحق للحمد على جميع أفعاله فلا يفعل إلا ما يستحق به حمدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can destroy people and replace them with a new creation, just as He first created them from nothing; this is easy for Him.
rows.anchor: { وما ذلك على الله بعزيز } أي ممتنع بل هو عليه هين يسير

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abu Bakr reads fa-ʿazaznā with a light z; the other readers use the doubled z form.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو بكر { فعززنا } بالتخفيف والباقون بتشديد الزاي

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وقالون عن نافع وزيد عن يعقوب
rows.claim: Abu Amr, Qalun from Nafi, and Zayd from Yaqub read the phrase with one unlengthened hamza.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وقالون عن نافع وزيد عن يعقوب أن ذكرتم بهمزة واحدة غير ممدودة

rows.speaker: ابن كثير ويعقوب ونافع
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Yaqub, and Nafi read the phrase with one lengthened hamza.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ويعقوب ونافع آن ذكرتم بهمزة واحدة ممدودة

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Ja'far reads one lengthened hamza and eases the second, with the verb light.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر أئن بهمزة واحدة مطولة والثانية ملينة مفتوحة ذكرتم مخففة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remaining readers pronounce two hamzas.
rows.anchor: والباقون أئن ذكرتم بهمزتين

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali says the doubled form means to strengthen and increase, while the light form means to overpower, as in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي: قال بعضهم عززنا قوينا وكثرنا وأما عززنا فغلبنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional particle receives the interrogative hamza; the answer is omitted and understood from their stated ill omen.
rows.anchor: إنما هي أن الجزاء دخلت عليها ألف الاستفهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tataiyarna means that they took the messengers as an ill omen; the word derives from Arabs' use of birds for omens, auspicious or inauspicious.
rows.anchor: وأصل تطيرنا تفعلنا من الطائر عند العرب الذي به يتشاءمون ويتيمنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the reading that opens the hamza, the meaning is because you reminded us, we took you as an ill omen; easing and full articulation of the hamza are discussed elsewhere.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ أن ذكرتم بفتح أن فالمعنى لأن ذكرتم تشاءمتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kulla shay'in is accusative under an understood verb, aḥṣaynā, which the explicit aḥṣaynāhu explains.
rows.anchor: { وكل شيء } منصوب بفعل مضمر يفسره هذا الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aṣḥāba al-qarya is apposition to mathalan; the first idh has an omitted governing phrase, and the later idh ars alnā is appositional to it.
rows.anchor: أصحاب القرية بدلا من مثلا. { إذ جاءها المرسلون } العامل في إذ محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After saying that the unbelievers do not believe, God says warning benefits only those who follow the Quran, since everyone has already received the warning.
rows.anchor: لما أخبر سبحانه عن أولئك الكفار أنهم لا يؤمنون وأنهم سواء عليهم الإنذار وترك الإنذار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can mean fearing God unseen from people, unlike a hypocrite, or fearing the unseen matters of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: أي في حال غيبته عن الناس بخلاف المنافق. وقيل: معناه وخشي الرحمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is to give such a person news of God's forgiveness and a reward free of impurities.
rows.anchor: أي ثواب خالص من الشوائب

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: Mujahid and Qatada take what people sent ahead to be their obedience and sins in worldly life.
rows.anchor: من طاعتهم ومعاصيهم في دار الدنيا عن مجاهد وقتادة

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i reads their آثار as deeds that leave a continuing effect, in contrast to the acts they sent ahead.
rows.anchor: أي ما يكون له أثر عن الجبائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is deeds people establish as a precedent after their death, whether good or bad, and others follow them in it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يعني بآثارهم أعمالهم التي صارت سنة بعدهم يقتدى فيها بهم

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Abu Sa'id reports that Banu Salima, living far from the mosque, complained to the Prophet about the distance; the verse was then revealed regarding their footsteps to prayer.
rows.anchor: ما رواه أبو سعيد الخدري أن بني سلمة كانوا في ناحية المدينة فشكوا إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو موسى
rows.claim: Abu Musa transmits the Prophet saying that those who walk the farthest to prayer receive the greatest reward; al-Bukhari and Muslim include the report in their Sahih collections.
rows.anchor: إن أعظم الناس أجرا في الصلاة أبعدهم إليها ممشى فأبعدهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Imam Mubin is the Preserved Tablet, a manifest register of all events, allowing angels to compare it with what happens and demonstrating God's detailed knowledge.
rows.anchor: أي وأحصينا وعددنا كل شيء من الحوادث في كتاب ظاهر وهو اللوح المحفوظ

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says it means the records of deeds, called clear because their marks do not wear away.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد به صحائف الأعمال وسمي ذلك مبينا لأنه لا يدرس أثره عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The city in the parable is Antioch according to the commentators; God sent messengers there, and its people denied them.
rows.anchor: وهذه القرية أنطاكية في قول المفسرين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the townspeople beat and imprisoned the first two messengers.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ضربوهما وسجنوهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The strengthened form means God reinforced and supported the two with a third messenger; it derives from might and protection, as in the proverb about the victor taking spoils.
rows.anchor: أي فقويناهما وشددنا ظهورهما برسول ثالث مأخوذ من العزة وهي القوة والمنعة

rows.speaker: شعبة
rows.claim: Shu'ba gives the first messengers' names as Shimon and John, and the third's as Paul.
rows.anchor: قال شعبة: كان اسم الرسولين شمعون ويوحنا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وكعب
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and Ka'b name the messengers Sadiq and Saduq, with Salum as the third.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وكعب: صادق وصدوق والثالث سلوم

rows.speaker: وهب وكعب
rows.claim: Another view identifies them as Jesus' apostles; God attributes them to Himself because Jesus sent them by His command.
rows.anchor: عن وهب وكعب قالا: وإنما أضافهم تعالى إلى نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers tell the people of the town that God has sent them to them.
rows.anchor: أي قالوا لهم يا أهل القرية إن الله أرسلنا إليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The townspeople argue that the messengers' shared humanity disqualifies them from prophethood, overlooking God's choice of people fit to bear its burden.
rows.anchor: فلا تصلحون للرسالة كما لا نصلح نحن لها

words: قَالُوا۟ رَبُّنَا يَعْلَمُ إِنَّآ إِلَيْكُم لَمُرْسَلُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After producing miracles that established the proof, the messengers invoke God's knowledge of their mission to urge the people to examine the miracles; the refusal carries a stern warning.
rows.anchor: وإنما قالوا ذلك بعد ما قامت الحجة بظهور المعجزة فلم يقبلوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means the messengers must deliver the message clearly; alternatively, they are not responsible for making people believe, which they cannot do.
rows.anchor: أي وليس يلزمنا إلا أداء الرسالة والتبليغ الظاهر. وقيل: معناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The townspeople say they took the messengers as an ill omen.
rows.anchor: أي تشاءمنا بكم { لئن لم تنتهوا } عما تدعونه من الرسالة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada explains their threat as stoning the messengers.
rows.anchor: بالحجارة عن قتادة. وقيل: معناه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid instead explains the threat as insulting the messengers.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه لنشتمنكم عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers reply that the real ill omen is the townspeople's persistence in unbelief; calling to monotheism brings blessing and good fortune.
rows.anchor: أي الشؤم كله معكم بإقامتكم على الكفر بالله تعالى فأما الدعاء إلى التوحيد

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة والمبرد
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda and al-Mubarrad explain ṭā'ir as one's share or allotment of good and evil.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معنى طائركم حظكم ونصيبكم من الخير والشر عن أبي عبيدة والمبرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A related verse says the Quran is a remembrance for Muhammad and his people.
rows.anchor: وإنه لذكر لك ولقومك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that the Quran clearly sets out proofs that lead a thoughtful person to know the truth by reason and religious teaching.
rows.anchor: ذي البيان الذي يؤدي إلى الحق ويهدي إلى الرشد لان فيه ذكر الأدلة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada takes it to mean a reminder or admonition for you.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ذي التذكر لكم عن قتادة

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i says the Quran mentions God, His unity, names and attributes, prophets and past nations, resurrection, and the rulings people need.
rows.anchor: فيه ذكر الله وتوحيده وأسماؤه الحسنى وصفاته العلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author supports the Quran's comprehensiveness with the statement that nothing has been omitted from the Book.
rows.anchor: ويؤيده قوله ما فرطنا في الكتاب من شيء

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada explains the Meccan unbelievers' ʿizza as pride, arrogant resistance to truth, and tribal zeal.
rows.anchor: أي في تكبر عن قبول الحق وحمية جاهلية عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that they had authority, capacity, and strength through God's enabling.
rows.anchor: وقيل: في ملكة واقتدار وقوة بتمكين الله إياهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their schism is enmity, disobedience, and opposition, since they disdain following the Prophet and seek to contradict him.
rows.anchor: أي عداوة وعصيان ومخالفة لأنهم يأنفون عن متابعتك ويطلبون مخالفتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier generations were destroyed for denying messengers and called for rescue only when destruction came, when escape was no longer possible.
rows.anchor: أي ليس الوقت حين منجى ولا فوت. وقيل: لات حين نداء ينجي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says they called at a time when calling could no longer save them.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة نادى القوم على غير حين النداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were astonished that a messenger from among them came from God to warn them against sins and the Fire.
rows.anchor: أي جاءهم رسول من أنفسهم مخوف من جهة الله تعالى يحذرهم المعاصي وينذرهم النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They called Muhammad a sorcerer and liar because he claimed to be God's messenger.
rows.anchor: حين يزعم أنه رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their question is an incredulous denial: Muhammad rejected their other gods and called them to worship God alone, which they found astonishing after worshipping many gods.
rows.anchor: هذا استفهام إنكار وتعجيب وذلك أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أبطل عبادة ما كانوا يعبدونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intilaq means going away easily; the same root is associated with an open face or good character.
rows.anchor: اللغة: الانطلاق الذهاب بسهولة ومنه طلاقة الوجه والخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ikhtilaq, fabrication, is close in meaning to lying, slander, and false invention.
rows.anchor: والاختلاق والفري والافتراء متقارب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Irtiqa means ascending step by step from a lower to a higher place; the quoted couplet uses it for climbing.
rows.anchor: لو لم يجد سلما ما كان مرتقيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asbab are means to reach an objective, and the means of heaven are its gates; Zuhayr's verse uses the expression.
rows.anchor: الأسباب جمع سبب والسبب ما يوصل به إلى المطلوب وأسباب السماوات أبوابها

rows.speaker: زهير
rows.claim: Zuhayr's line speaks of people who fear death's paths and would try to reach heaven by a ladder.
rows.anchor: ومن هاب أسباب المنايا ينلنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In theologians' usage, a cause brings about an essence, whereas an ʿilla brings about an attribute.
rows.anchor: والفرق بين السبب والعلة في عرف المتكلمين أن السبب ما يوجب ذاتا والعلة ما يوجب صفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An here is explanatory, meaning that is, go.
rows.anchor: أن هذه هي التي تسمى المفسرة بمعنى أي امشوا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj also allows an implied bi, meaning by saying, Go.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: ويجوز أن يكون تقديره بأن امشوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nobles leave their gathering at Abu Talib's house, telling one another to persist in worshipping their gods and bear hardship for their religion.
rows.anchor: هذا تمام الحكاية عن الكفار الذي تقدم ذكرهم أي وانطلق الأشراف منهم

rows.speaker: عقبة بن أبي معيط
rows.claim: A report identifies Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt as the one who said to persist in worship of the gods.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن القائل لذلك عقبة بن أبي معيط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that this is a plot or matter intended against them.
rows.anchor: { لشيء يراد } أي أمر يراد بنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that this is corruption in the land, soon to bring destruction and free them of it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه إن هذا فساد في الأرض وعن قريب ينزل به الهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation is their fear that leaving idol worship would remove blessings or bring hardship, since they believed the idols caused drought and distress.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن هذا الأمر يراد بنا من زوال نعمة أو نزول شدة

words: مَا سَمِعْنَا بِهَٰذَا فِى ٱلْمِلَّةِ ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the last religion means Christianity, the latest religion, whose adherents do not profess God's oneness because they say He is three.
rows.anchor: يعنون في النصرانية لأنها آخر الملل عن ابن عباس قال إن النصارى لا يوحدون

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: Mujahid and Qatada take it to mean the religion of Quraysh in their own time.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يعنون ملة قريش أي في ملة زماننا هذا عن مجاهد وقتادة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan understands the phrase as saying they had not heard that this would happen at the end of time.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه ما سمعنا بأن هذا يكون في آخر الزمان عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call Muhammad's teaching a fabricated lie.
rows.anchor: { إلا اختلاق } أي تخرص وكذب وافتعال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They object that the Quran and prophethood were given to Muhammad rather than to someone older or more distinguished than they are.
rows.anchor: كيف أنزل على محمد القرآن من بيننا وليس بأكبر سنا منا ولا بأعظم شرفا

words: بَلْ هُمْ فِى شَكٍّ مِّن ذِكْرِى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answers that their objection is driven by doubt about His revelation; they have not yet tasted the punishment that awaits them.
rows.anchor: أي ليس يحملهم على هذا القول إلا الشك في الذكر الذي أنزلته على رسولي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question asks whether they hold the keys to prophethood and can assign it; the choice belongs to the Mighty Bestower, who selects servants as wisdom requires.
rows.anchor: أبأيديهم مفاتيح النبوة والرسالة فيضعونها حيث شاؤوا أي إنها ليست بأيديهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yanabiʿ are places where water springs forth; nabaʿ describes water gushing from a place.
rows.anchor: الينابيع جمع ينبوع وهو الموضع الذي ينبع منه الماء. يقال: نبع الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zarʿ is vegetation without a trunk, shajar has a trunk and branches, and nabat covers both generally.
rows.anchor: والزرع ما ينبت على غير ساق والشجر ما له ساق وأغصان والنبات يعم الجميع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A plant heaves when it dries and reaches the end of its dryness; hutam is broken straw or grass, from breaking dry things.
rows.anchor: وهاج النبت يهيج هيجا إذا جف وبلغ نهايته في اليبوسة والحطام فتات التبن والحشيش

rows.speaker: النضر
rows.claim: Al-Nadr says al-Hatim in Mecca names a piece of the Kaaba's stone by the spout, left crushed after the House was raised.
rows.anchor: قال النضر: لأن البيت رفع وترك ذلك محطوما وهو حجر الكعبة مما يلي الميزاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative clause with man is the subject and its predicate is omitted, understood as is one whose chest God expanded like one whose heart hardened by abandoning remembrance?
rows.anchor: من مع صلته مبتدأ والخبر محذوف تقديره أفمن شرح الله صدره كمن قسا قلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase can refer to shrinking at the mention of God, with qasat min dhikr Allah understood as hardening when people mention God.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون تشمئز عند ذكر الله. فيقال: قست من ذكر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kitaban is accusative as an appositional substitute for the best discourse.
rows.anchor: { كتابا } منصوب لأنه بدل من قوله أحسن الحديث

words: أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ أَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءًۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sends rain into the earth as springs, then brings forth crops of varied kinds and colors, which dry, yellow, and crumble.
rows.anchor: { فسلكه } أي فأدخل ذلك الماء { ينابيع في الأرض }

words: إِنَّ فِى ذَٰلِكَ لَذِكْرَىٰ لِأُو۟لِى ٱلْأَلْبَٰبِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Diverse plants produced from one water and carried through successive states remind sound minds of the Creator and establish the truth of first creation, resurrection, and return.
rows.anchor: لتذكيرا لذوي العقول السليمة إذا تفكروا في ذلك عرفوا الصانع المحدث وعلموا صحة الابتداء والبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's opening of the breast means widening the heart to accept Islam and remain steadfast in it; the address is to the Prophet though it applies to all morally responsible people.
rows.anchor: يخاطب نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم وإن كان المراد جميع المكلفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first of three means by which the breast is opened is the strength of God's proofs, a benefit specific to scholars.
rows.anchor: وشرح الصدر يكون بثلاثة أشياء: أحدها: بقوة الأدلة التي نصبها الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second means is God's graces, renewed for a person continually.
rows.anchor: والثاني: بالألطاف التي تتجدد له حالا بعد حال كما قال سبحانه
